core_obligations: Orbit finiteness and the invariant open W' (proof lines 5153-5164): s finite locally free has finite fibres, so the orbit {u_1, ..., u_n} is finite and contains u; for affine W containing the orbit, t(Z) with Z = R \ s^{-1}(W) cap t^{-1}(W) is closed because t is finite (standing hypothesis), making W' = U \ t(Z) an R-invariant open contained in W and containing the orbit.

The norm function (proof lines 5165-5192): 00DS gives f with orbit subset D(f) subset W'; since s^{-1}(W') subset t^{-1}(W), the norm g = Norm_s(t-sharp f) is defined on W', is nonzero at u, and D(g) is precisely the set of points whose entire R-equivalence class keeps f nonzero, hence R-invariant and affine; the final chain shows u in D(g) subset U.
